rationale: This is a simple additive blend of two separately well-documented anomalies (R&D intensity and net external financing) with no genuine conditioning, so a positive result would be almost entirely attributable to the known components rather than to any cross-theme interaction.

The construction is internally consistent and the sign is right, though it sits close to the known stock-financed-acquisition underperformance result, and the claim that the rank product "fires only when both conditions hold" overstates what a monotone product of ranks actually does.

The debt-plus-goodwill fragility mechanism is coherent and the sign matches the expression, but COALESCE(gdwl, intan) silently mixes two economically different quantities across firms (goodwill additions vs. total intangible changes), which contaminates cross-sectional comparability and partly overlaps the asset-growth anomaly.

This is a near-duplicate of "Internally Funded Innovation Intensity" in a different wrapper and amounts to the R&D-intensity anomaly plus the composite-share-issuance anomaly (Pontiff-Woodgate) added together, i.e., a rediscovery of two published effects rather than a new interaction.

target_name: External Finance per Unit of Intangible Capital
rationale: With intan+xrd near zero for a large share of firms and a numerator that changes sign, the cross-sectional dispersion will be driven by the inverse of intangible intensity and by denominator blowups (1% winsorization is far too mild), so the signal is a noisy re-scaling of the known net-external-financing anomaly.

This is a genuinely conditional, sign-flipping interaction whose hypothesis, expression, and expected sign are mutually consistent; the main risks are that SIGN discards trend magnitude and that revt/MA(xrd,3) restricts coverage to R&D reporters, both of which are testable rather than disqualifying.
